questions.sec: FLD features, NASH histology, risk-factor table and 2-hit progression
questions.q: How is NAFLD defined under 'Features' of Fatty Liver Disease?
opts: Macrovesicular fat / steatosis in ≥ 5% of hepatocytes
questions.exp: 'NAFLD : macrovesicular fat / steatosis ≥5% hepatocytes (Non alcoholic FLD)'. The micrograph caption reads 'macrovesicular fat in NAFLD'. (Book p1030)

questions.sec: FLD features, NASH histology, risk-factor table and 2-hit progression
questions.q: NAFLD splits into two groups — match — 1) 80% 2) 20% … A) Fatty liver + inflammation = NASH B) Isolated fatty liver (IFL)
questions.exp: 80% Isolated fatty liver (IFL); 20% Fatty liver + Inflammation: NASH (non-alcoholic steatohepatitis). (Book p1030)

questions.sec: FLD features, NASH histology, risk-factor table and 2-hit progression
questions.q: Four histological components branch from NASH. Which is NOT one of them?
questions.exp: Branches: Ballooning change; Degree of steatosis; Lobular inflammation; Chicken-wire fibrosis (Zone 3). (Book p1030)

questions.sec: FLD features, NASH histology, risk-factor table and 2-hit progression
questions.q: Fill up: The fibrosis pattern of NASH is '______ fibrosis (Zone ______)'.
questions.exp: 'Chicken-wire fibrosis (Zone 3)'. (Book p1030)

questions.sec: FLD features, NASH histology, risk-factor table and 2-hit progression
questions.q: Risk-factor table, column 'Common conditions with established association' — which is NOT in that column?
questions.exp: Column 1: Obesity, T2DM/insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, metabolic syndrome, PCOS, starvation/rapid weight loss, ↓ adiponectin, leptin resistance. Hypothyroidism is in column 2. (Book p1030)

questions.sec: FLD features, NASH histology, risk-factor table and 2-hit progression
questions.q: Judge from column 1: I Adiponectin levels are printed as decreased. II Leptin is printed as deficient.
questions.exp: '↓ Adiponectin levels' and 'Leptin Resistance' (not deficiency). (Book p1030)

questions.sec: FLD features, NASH histology, risk-factor table and 2-hit progression
questions.q: Column 'Other conditions associated with NAFLD' — which is NOT listed?
questions.exp: Column 2: Hypothyroidism, OSA, Hypopituitarism, Hypogonadism, Pancreatoduodenal resection, Psoriasis. (Book p1030)

questions.sec: FLD features, NASH histology, risk-factor table and 2-hit progression
questions.q: Match — 1) T2DM / insulin resistance 2) Hypopituitarism 3) Hypogonadism … A) Other conditions associated B) Common established association
questions.exp: T2DM/insulin resistance is column 1; hypopituitarism and hypogonadism are column 2. (Book p1030)

questions.sec: FLD features, NASH histology, risk-factor table and 2-hit progression
questions.q: Drugs column — which drug is NOT printed among the six NAFLD-associated drugs?
questions.exp: Drugs: L-asparaginase, Bleomycin, Tetracycline, Griseofulvin, Valproate, Amiodarone. (Book p1030)

questions.sec: FLD features, NASH histology, risk-factor table and 2-hit progression
questions.q: Fill up: NASH progression follows a ______-hit hypothesis; the 1st hit is ______.
questions.exp: '2 hit hypothesis — Normal liver —1st hit: Risk factors→ NASH —2nd hit: unknown R/F→ Cirrhosis'. (Book p1030)

questions.sec: FLD features, NASH histology, risk-factor table and 2-hit progression
questions.q: What proportion of NASH patients progress to cirrhosis, and over what period?
questions.exp: '2nd hit : unknown R/F — 10–15% pts over 15 yrs → Cirrhosis'. (Book p1030)

questions.sec: FLD features, NASH histology, risk-factor table and 2-hit progression
questions.q: In the progression diagram an arrow runs directly from NASH to HCC, bypassing cirrhosis, labelled 'Only in NASH & ______'. Complete it.
questions.exp: 'Only in NASH & Hep B virus infection' — HCC without intervening cirrhosis. Cirrhosis itself branches to portal hypertension, liver failure and HCC. (Book p1030)

questions.sec: Clinical features, investigations, fibroscan figure and enzyme algorithm
questions.q: Clinical features table, 'Symptoms' column — which is NOT printed?
questions.exp: Symptoms: Vague RUQ pain, Fatigue, malaise. (Book p1031)

questions.sec: Clinical features, investigations, fibroscan figure and enzyme algorithm
questions.q: 'Sign' column — hepatomegaly, then four rare signs each bracketed with its meaning. Match — 1) Splenomegaly 2) Spider angiomata 3) Ascites … A) Decompensation B) PHTN C) Liver failure
questions.exp: Rare: Splenomegaly (PHTN), Spider angiomata (Liver failure), Palmar erythema, Ascites (Decompensation). (Book p1031)

questions.sec: Clinical features, investigations, fibroscan figure and enzyme algorithm
questions.q: Judge: I Hepatomegaly is the routine sign of NAFLD. II Palmar erythema is listed among the rare signs.
questions.exp: Sign: Hepatomegaly; Rare: splenomegaly, spider angiomata, palmar erythema, ascites. (Book p1031)

questions.sec: Clinical features, investigations, fibroscan figure and enzyme algorithm
questions.q: Investigations 1–4 — match — 1) Biopsy 2) S. Ferritin 3) Imaging 4) Enzymes … A) Elevated B) ALT, AST C) Inflammatory changes D) USG → MR elastography > transient elastography
questions.exp: 1. Biopsy: inflammatory changes; 2. S. Ferritin: elevated; 3. Imaging: USG → MR elastography > transient elastography; 4. Enzymes: ALT, AST. (Book p1031)

questions.sec: Clinical features, investigations, fibroscan figure and enzyme algorithm
questions.q: Which imaging modality is ranked higher on this page: MR elastography or transient elastography?
questions.exp: 'USG → MR Elastography > Transient Elastography'. (Book p1031)

questions.sec: Clinical features, investigations, fibroscan figure and enzyme algorithm
questions.q: Liver fibroscan figure — match — 1) Vs = 1.1 m/s 2) Vs = 1.7 m/s 3) Vs = 3.6 m/s … A) ~ 9 kPa B) ~ 40 kPa C) ~ 3 kPa
questions.exp: Panels: Vs 1.1 m/s ~3 kPa; Vs 1.7 m/s ~9 kPa; Vs 3.6 m/s ~40 kPa, above the F0–F4 scale. (Book p1031)

questions.sec: Clinical features, investigations, fibroscan figure and enzyme algorithm
questions.q: The fibroscan figure shows a staging strip from ______ to ______ and the probe illustration cites an explored volume of ______ × ______ cm.
questions.exp: Strip F0 F1 F2 F3 F4; the probe inset labels 'Volumen explorado' 2.5 cm and 4 cm. (Book p1031)

questions.sec: Clinical features, investigations, fibroscan figure and enzyme algorithm
questions.q: ALT/AST algorithm: enzymes are normal. What is the printed conclusion?
questions.exp: 'ALT, AST → Normal → IFL'. (Book p1031)

questions.sec: Clinical features, investigations, fibroscan figure and enzyme algorithm
questions.q: Enzymes ↑↑ (<150 U/L) — match — 1) AST < ALT 2) AST > ALT … A) Cirrhosis B) NASH (risk & cirrhosis)
questions.exp: '↑↑ (<150 U/L) → AST<ALT → NASH (Risk & cirrhosis); AST>ALT → Cirrhosis'. (Book p1031)

questions.sec: Clinical features, investigations, fibroscan figure and enzyme algorithm
questions.q: A 45-year-old obese diabetic has ALT 110, AST 70 U/L. Following the algorithm, fibroscan is done and stiffness is markedly raised (↑↑). What is the final printed label?
questions.exp: AST<ALT → NASH → Fibroscan → (N) NASH without cirrhosis / ↑↑ NASH with cirrhosis. (Book p1031)

questions.sec: Supportive treatment and drugs
questions.q: Supportive treatment of NASH — what weight-loss target and exercise prescription are printed?
opts: Weight loss 10% over 6 months; exercise 30–45 min/day × 5 days/week
Weight loss 5% over 3 months; exercise 60 min/day × 7 days/week
Weight loss 15% over 12 months; exercise 20 min/day × 3 days/week
Weight loss 10% over 1 month; exercise 30 min × 2 days/week
questions.exp: 'Weight loss : 10% over 6 months. Exercise : 30 – 45 minutes / day × 5 day / wk.' (Book p1032)

questions.sec: Supportive treatment and drugs
questions.q: Fill up the third supportive bullet: '______ fatty acids, ______'.
questions.exp: 'Omega 3 fatty acids, caffeine.' (Book p1032)

questions.sec: Supportive treatment and drugs
questions.q: Vitamin E is the printed DOC for NASH. What dose is given?
questions.exp: 'DOC : Vitamin E — 800–1000 unit/day.' (Book p1032)

questions.sec: Supportive treatment and drugs
questions.q: Judge the Vitamin E sub-bullets: I Improves NASH. II Its efficacy in cirrhosis is unknown. III Takes about 2 years to show effect.
opts: I true, II and III false
I and III true, II false
I and II true, III false
questions.exp: 'improves NASH, unknown efficacy in cirrhosis' and 'takes ~2 years to show effect'. (Book p1032)

questions.sec: Supportive treatment and drugs
questions.q: Saroglitazar (4 mg) works by which mechanism, per the book?
questions.exp: 'Saroglitazar (4mg) : Dual PPAR-α + PPAR-γ agonist.' (Book p1032)

questions.sec: Supportive treatment and drugs
questions.q: Match — 1) Pioglitazone 2) Oral semaglutide 3) Saroglitazar … A) GLP-1 RA B) PPAR-γ agonist (may be tried) C) Dual PPAR-α + γ agonist
questions.exp: Pioglitazone PPAR-γ agonist (may be tried); Oral semaglutide GLP-1 RA (receptor agonist); Saroglitazar dual PPAR-α+γ. (Book p1032)

units.title: NAFLD definition, NASH histology, risk factors and progression
units.guide: Macrovesicular fat ≥5% hepatocytes; 80% IFL vs 20% NASH; ballooning, steatosis degree, lobular inflammation, chicken-wire zone-3 fibrosis; established (obesity, T2DM/IR, dyslipidemia, MetS, PCOS, starvation, ↓adiponectin, leptin resistance), other (hypothyroid, OSA, hypopituitarism, hypogonadism, pancreatoduodenal resection, psoriasis), drugs (L-asparaginase, bleomycin, tetracycline, griseofulvin, valproate, amiodarone); 2-hit, 10–15% over 15 yrs, direct HCC only in NASH & HBV.

units.title: Clinical features, investigations, fibroscan and the ALT/AST algorithm
units.guide: Vague RUQ pain, fatigue, malaise; hepatomegaly; rare splenomegaly (PHTN), spider angiomata (liver failure), palmar erythema, ascites (decompensation); biopsy, ferritin, USG → MR elastography > transient elastography, ALT/AST; Vs 1.1/1.7/3.6 m/s ≈ 3/9/40 kPa, F0–F4; normal → IFL; <150 AST<ALT → NASH → fibroscan N/↑↑; AST>ALT → cirrhosis.

units.title: Treatment: lifestyle and drugs
units.guide: 10% weight loss over 6 months; 30–45 min × 5 days/week; omega-3, caffeine; vitamin E DOC 800–1000 U/day, improves NASH, unknown in cirrhosis, ~2 years; saroglitazar 4 mg dual PPAR-α/γ; pioglitazone PPAR-γ may be tried; oral semaglutide GLP-1 RA.
